```{python}
from fairdatanow import DataViewer, data_now, login, filters
from read_spx import get_spectrum 
import re 
import os

url = "https://laboppad.nl/ukiyo-e-world" 
```

```{python}
spx_files = DataViewer(login(url), **filters(search='.*RV-1-4468-544.*[.]spx', use_regex=True)).download_filtered()
```

Ok, let's learn first how to use plotly to make a figure... 

```{python}
spx_files
```

```{python}
titles = [os.path.basename(spx) for spx in spx_files]
titles
```

```{python}
spectra = [get_spectrum(spx) for spx in spx_files]
```

```{python}
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
import plotly.graph_objects as go

fig = make_subplots(rows=len(spectra), cols=1, shared_xaxes=True)#, shared_yaxes=True)

for i, df in enumerate(spectra): 
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(x=df['energies'], y=df['intensities'], mode='lines', name=titles[i]),
        row=i+1, col=1, 
    )

fig.update_layout(height=1000, 
                  width=1500, 
                  title_text="Side By Side Subplots",
                  xaxis=dict(tickmode='linear', tick0=0, dtick=1))
fig.update_yaxes(range=[0, 4000])
fig.update_xaxes(range=[0, 20])

fig.show()
```
